f.title: A column title the file carries twice is read from its first column, silently. A mapping-box answer is remembered by title, so the next import of the same layout reads the wrong column and counts subtotals twice
f.area: W1 import: header search, mapping box, ACEDB.cols
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceFindHeader (line 14851 `if(n && !(n in at)) at[n]=i`; line 14859 remembered answers resolved through `at[aceTitleN(mem[F.f])]`); aceImportGo stores ACEDB.cols[sig].map as the title text
f.scenario: Two cases. (a) By title: the file has two columns whose titles reduce to the same string, for example column A also titled 'Rollup Value?' while the real flags are in H. (b) Remembered: 'Rollup Value?' is renamed 'Flag' and column A is also 'Flag'. The person picks H in the mapping box; the first import reads H. The next import of the same layout (same signature) is read without asking: the stored answer is the title 'Flag', which resolves to column A (the Index column). Either way no Rollup Value? = Yes row is found, the $3,000,000 subtotal is kept beside its two parts, and FY27 reads $6,000,000. The status says 'No row left out'. The only signal is 'remembered for this layout · A' inside the folded 'Columns read' list.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p1-dup-title.mjs prints: '1st import: rollup col { t: 'Flag', c: 'H', how: 'asked' } kept FY27 $ 3000000 lines 2 rollup reason {rows:1, v:{2027:3000000}}', then '2nd import: box open false rollup col {t:'Flag', c:'A', how:'remembered'} kept FY27 $ 6000000 lines 3 rollup reason null'. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p12-dup-title-bytitle.mjs (by title) prints: 'rollup read from column A (the real one is H) · kept FY27 6000000 (true: 3,000,000) · named 0'.
f.fix: Remember the column INDEX with the title (`map:{roll:{t:'Flag', i:7}}`). The signature is identical, so the index is exact. When resolving, use the index only if that column's normalised title still matches. Separately, in aceFindHeader count each normalised title. When a field's title, or a remembered title, occurs more than once in the header, push the field to `need` (ask) instead of taking the first occurrence. Add a fixture with a duplicated title to the W1 block.

votes.why:
I read the code at 2bafb12 and it does what the finding says. aceFindHeader (line 14851) keeps only the first column for each normalised title: `if(n && !(n in at)) at[n]=i`. A remembered answer is resolved through that same map (`at[aceTitleN(mem[F.f])]`, line 14859). The mapping box itself picks by index (aceColApply sets `H.col[f]=+v`), but aceImportGo saves the TITLE of the column picked (`map[F.f]=t`, then `ACEDB.cols[H.sig]={map:m,...}`). The index the person chose is never kept.

I wrote and ran my own probe against the 2bafb12 board: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-0-0/probe-dup.mjs. The file was built by the board's own buildXlsx and driven through importAce and the rendered box. Fixture: a $3M subtotal row and its two parts ($1M, $2M).

(b) Remembered. I titled 'Rollup Value?' (H) 'Flag' and also titled 'Sub Index' (B) 'Flag'. The box listed both, as 'B · Flag' and 'H · Flag'. I picked H.
- First import: map.roll = H/asked, the rollup row left out, 2 lines, FY27 $3,000,000.
- ACEDB.cols stored `{roll:'Flag'}`.
- Second import of the same layout: no box, map.roll = B/remembered, rollup reason null, 3 lines, FY27 $6,000,000. The status said 'No row left out. Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason.'

(a) By title. With B titled 'Rollup Value?' and H 'Rollup value', the file was read from B by title: FY27 $6,000,000, no box, the same clean status.

The only signal is the column letter, inside the folded 'Columns read, by title' details (line 17797).

Neither the contract nor notes-W1 decides how duplicate titles are handled. The contract's tie rule covers rows (first sheet, then first row), not columns. Item 132 says 'nothing is guessed', and that the answer is remembered 'for files laid out the same way'. Taking the first of two same-titled columns is a guess, and overriding the person's explicit pick on the next import of the identical layout breaks that promise.

It is reachable by a real person, through the ordinary import and the mapping box, with an .xlsx whose header repeats a title after normalisation. Brad says the ACE files add columns year over year.
votes.corrected:
The finding holds as stated. Two refinements:
1. Severity is closer to moderate than major. It needs a header in which two columns' titles normalise alike. The 2026 header Brad listed in item 132 shows no such pair, so it is a latent hazard for a future or reworked file, not today's file. When it fires, though, it silently changes the money: a subtotal is kept and FY27 is doubled.
2. On the fix: storing an index alone would bend the contract's 'nothing is read by position'. Two contract-consistent routes:
   - Ask in the mapping box whenever a field's title, or a remembered title, occurs more than once in the header.
   - Remember the index only as a tiebreak among columns whose normalised title still matches.

Line numbers 14851 and 14859 are at 2bafb12. At the worktree's HEAD, e2f6813, the same code is at 14902 and 14909, unchanged.

votes.why:
I read the code at 2bafb12. aceFindHeader (prioritization-board-grid.html line 14851) builds `at` with `if(n && !(n in at)) at[n]=i`, so a normalised title the header carries twice always resolves to its first column. aceImportGo (about line 17686) stores the answer from the mapping box as the title text (`map[F.f]=t`, then `ACEDB.cols[H.sig]={map:m,...}`). On the next import, line 14859 resolves that title through the same `at[aceTitleN(mem[F.f])]`.

I wrote my own probe, without the reviewer's lib.mjs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-0-1/probe.mjs. It imports through the real importAce, with a workbook from the board's own buildXlsx. The fixture is a $3M subtotal row (Rollup Yes) and its $1M and $2M parts.
- CONTROL: the rollup is read from G and FY27 keeps 3,000,000.
- (a) Column A is also titled 'Rollup Value?'. The rollup is read from A (how: title), FY27 keeps 6,000,000, and there are 3 lines and no rollup reason. The box is not opened. The status says "No row left out. Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason."
- (b) The rollup column is renamed 'Flag' and A is also 'Flag'. The box asks, and its own options read "A · Flag" and "G · Flag". The person picks G, and the first import reads G (3,000,000). The board stores `{map:{roll:'Flag'}}`. The second import of the identical layout opens no box, reads A (how: remembered) and keeps 6,000,000. The only sign is the report's folded "Columns read" row, "Rollup Value? Flag A remembered for this layout".

Neither the contract nor notes-W1 decides anything about duplicate titles. The contract says "nothing is read by position" and "a file laid out the same way is read without asking". Notes-W1 says "nothing is guessed". Replacing the person's explicit pick of G with A on the same layout breaks that. So does silently taking the first of two equal titles. This is a real defect, not a documented decision.

Reachable: through Data › Import Annual Cost Estimate, with an ordinary .xlsx whose header repeats a title. Brad says ACE layouts change and add columns. No hostile input is needed.
votes.corrected:
The defect is confirmed, with three limits.

1. The file Brad meets today does not trigger it. The 2026 header (as rebuilt in the audit-other W1 fixture, WBS in Z) has no repeated titles. It needs a later file whose header repeats a title, with the wrong copy in the earlier column.
2. A repeated title to the RIGHT of the real column is harmless; I checked: rollup read from G, FY27 3,000,000. Only the first occurrence is ever read.
3. The consequence depends on which field is misread. For Rollup Value? it is double-counted subtotals: FY27 $6M where it should be $3M, and conservation still "ties", so nothing flags it. For other fields it would misfile or leave out rows. Major is defensible for money read silently wrong. It is reachable only when a layout repeats a title.

On the fix:
- Storing the column index with the title is exact under an identical signature. The signature is every normalised title in order, so the suggested "title still matches" re-check can never fail; it is harmless.
- It changes the contract's stated shape, `map:{field:'title as in file'}`, so the contract and notes need the same update.
- Separately, a field (or a remembered title) whose normalised title occurs more than once in the header should be asked about in the box, not taken from the first column.

f.title: The Data card's 'Import report…' line writes the sum of each reason's `rows` unescaped. A board file can put markup on the page as it opens
f.area: W1 import report: escape where drawn
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html syncBtns, I.acer (line 30733): `...+' lines kept · '+out+' row'...` where `out` is reduced from `(R.reasons[x]||{}).rows`
f.scenario: A saved board, folder copy or full-import file carries ACEDB.sets['2026ACE'].rep.reasons.dtype.rows = ''. The file passes the import check: inWalk only length-checks strings. When the board opens, render → syncBtns writes the Data list into #uiHold, and the reduce turns 0 + that text into '0', drawn raw. No click is needed. The hostile sweep plants `rows:1` (a number) and so cannot see this.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p7-acer-sink.mjs prints: 'the saved board passes the import check: passes', 'before any call, right after opening: true' (document.getElementById('pwn') exists) and 'menu line: … 2026ACE: 1 lines kept · 0 rows left out, with reasons'.
f.fix: Count with numbers: `a+(+((R.reasons[x]||{}).rows)||0)`, and draw `esc(out)`. In hostile.mjs, plant text (not a number) in rep.reasons[k].rows, rep.kept.lines/rows and rep.years, so the sweep can catch this class.

votes.why: I confirmed this at 2bafb12 by reading the code and by writing my own probe that goes through a real door. Code: in syncBtns, `I.acer` (lines 30729-30733) sums `out` as `a+((R.reasons[x]||{}).rows||0)`. If `rows` is text, that becomes string concatenation ('0'+text). `out` is then written into `mi()`'s `sub`, and `mi()` (line 30532) puts `sub` into the button markup as it is. `esc()` is applied only to `k` and `kept.lines`. The import check does not catch it. `inWalk` checks a string's length only, and `inShapeWhy` has no rule for an estimate's `rep`. `aceFingerprint` covers `appn` and the number of lines, not `rep`. My probe is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-1-0/probe1.mjs. The original probe only booted the crafted HTML, and a crafted HTML file is code anyway. Mine does this instead: - A sender's board plants `rep.reasons.dtype.rows = ''` and saves with `buildSavedHtml()`. - A separate receiver board runs `inboundCheck` on the file: it passes. - The receiver takes the file through `fullImportText` (Imports & exports › Import a full board), which returned true. - prio27acedb then holds the string. - I rebooted the receiver's own program with that browser storage, to stand in for the import's `location.reload()`. With no click at all, `#pwn` exists inside `span.sub` of the Data card's "Import report…" button. The line reads `2026ACE: 1 lines kept · 0 rows left out, with reasons`. The report box itself draws the same value escaped (`esc(x.rows)`); only the menu line is raw. Other ways in: the ordinary board import's `importStores` takes any estimate set the board does not hold, and the shared folder's estimate pull does not catch it either, because the fingerprint ignores `rep`. In Chromium the handler would run. The board's CSP has `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` (the board needs it for its own handlers), and an image that fails to load fires `onerror`. The rule it breaks is required, not a judgment call. CLAUDE.md v2.00 says a value from a file is escaped where it is drawn, and contract.md's "rules that bite here" names escape where drawn. Nothing in notes-W1.md decides to leave this line raw. The finding is also right that the hostile sweep cannot see it: hostile.mjs line 124 plants `rows:1`, a number. Severity major is fair: markup from another person's file lands on the page as the board opens.
votes.corrected: The finding stands as written. One precision: the strongest way to reproduce it is not opening the crafted HTML directly, which is code anyway. It is a colleague's board file taken in through Imports & exports › Import a full board, or through the ordinary board import, which takes any estimate set the board does not hold. After the import's reload, the board's own program draws the markup from browser storage into the Data card's "Import report…" hint, with no click. The fix as proposed is right: count with `+(…rows)||0` and draw `esc(out)`. hostile.mjs should plant text in `rep.reasons[k].rows`, `rep.kept.lines` and `rep.kept.rows`.

votes.why: I tried to refute this and could not. The finding is confirmed at 2bafb12. **The code.** In `syncBtns`, `I.acer` (prioritization-board-grid.html, lines 30729-30733) sums `(R.reasons[x]||{}).rows||0` with a reduce that starts at 0. It writes that sum, `out`, into the item's hint without escaping it, while the lines-kept figure beside it is escaped (`esc((R.kept||{}).lines||0)`). `mi()` at line 30532 puts `sub` into the markup raw. The report box itself does escape the same field (`esc(x.rows)`, about line 17816), so the menu line is an escaped sink's sibling that was missed. The contract (recovery/v212/contract.md, line 210) and CLAUDE.md v2.00 both require escaping where a value is drawn. Neither notes-W1.md nor notes-W3.md records a decision to leave it. **The import check lets it through.** `inWalk` only checks a string's length, and `inShapeWhy` has no rule for an estimate's `rep`. `importStores` takes a set this board does not hold, whole, with its report (about line 11374). **My own probe** (verify-w1-parse-1-1/probe-acer.mjs). I saved an ordinary board, then hand-edited its pubState so that `rep.reasons.dtype.rows` holds ``. - The import check passes the edited file. - **Door 1, Import a full board:** `fullImportText` returns true. After the reload, with no click, `#pwn` is on the page inside the Data item's `span.sub`. The menu line reads `2026ACE: 1 lines kept · 0 rows left out, with reasons`. - **Door 2, the ordinary Import of a board file:** the harness reaches `importStores` through the shell path; on a populated board, typing ALL in `consTakeApply` reaches the same call. The `rows` value arrives as a string and `#pwn` is drawn. It is drawn again when that browser reopens the board. - **Controls:** with `rows` set to 3 the line reads "3 rows left out" and draws no markup. The report box shows the same planted value escaped (`<img…`). **In Chromium** (verify-w1-parse-1-1/probe-browser-run.mjs), the edited file opened under the board's own Content-Security-Policy gives `#pwn` on the page and `window.__pw === 1`. The handler runs because `script-src` is `'unsafe-inline'`, and no CSP message appeared. **Why the hostile sweep missed it.** tools/export-audit/hostile.mjs line 124 plants `reasons:{pmo:{rows:1,…}}`, a number, so it cannot reach this sink. The proposed fix stands: add the counts as numbers (`+(…rows)||0`) and draw `esc(out)`; in hostile.mjs, plant text rather than numbers in the report's count fields.
votes.corrected: No correction to the finding. One addition: it is reachable through two real import doors, not only by opening the file. Import a full board, then the reload, draws the markup with no click. So does the ordinary Import of a board file, through importStores (consTakeApply with ALL on a populated board). The planted handler runs in Chromium under the board's own CSP: window.__pw was 1.

f.title: The import report draws rep.years unescaped: the year picker's option values and labels, and the 'dollars in FY…' line
f.area: W1 import report: escape where drawn
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceRepBody, line 17795 ('dollars in FY'+yrs[0]+'–FY'+yrs[yrs.length-1]) and line 17807 ('<option value="'+y+'"…>FY'+y)
f.scenario: A board file whose estimate report has years: ['2027">'], with total.v holding the same key so the year survives the `R.total.v[y]` filter, passes the import check. The person opens Data › Import report… and the element is built in the page.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p8-rep-years-sink.mjs prints 'passes the import check: passes' and, after aceRepShow('2026ACE'), 'injected element on the page: true'.
f.fix: Read the years as numbers at the top of aceRepBody: `yrs=(R.years||[]).map(Number).filter(function(y){ return Number.isInteger(y) && (R.total.v||{})[y]; })`, or draw `esc(y)` in all three places.

votes.why: The finding holds at 2bafb12. I reproduced it through the board's real import doors and its real menu button, not by booting a saved file directly. **The code.** `aceRepBody` (prioritization-board-grid.html:17767) builds `yrs` from `R.years`, keeping only years that `(R.total.v||{})[y]` makes truthy, and writes the years into markup without `esc()` in two places: - the "dollars in FY'+yrs[0]+'–FY'+yrs[yrs.length-1]" line (17795); - the year picker's options, `'
votes.corrected: Unchanged in substance. One detail: in jsdom the two injected elements both come from the "dollars in FY…" line; the parser drops markup inside a `<select>`, so the option value only shows as a broken attribute. The read line alone is enough to inject the element, and both places need `esc()` (or integer years).

votes.why: I confirmed it, by a stronger route than the original probe. That probe opened the crafted board HTML directly, which proves nothing on its own: a hand-made HTML file can carry its own script. My probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-2-1/probe.mjs) takes the real path a person meets: 1. Board A saves a file whose 2026ACE estimate has rep.years = ['2027">', 2027] and total.v keyed by that string. 2. A different board B checks the file: inboundCheck passes it. inWalk only refuses IN_KEY_BAD keys, `years` is not in IN_VAL_KEYS, and no rule looks at markup in ordinary text. 3. B takes it through the whole-board import door: fullImportText returns true and writes prio27acedb with the hostile year. 4. The board reopens from that storage. The boot pick keeps rep as stored; nothing normalises it. 5. A click on the Data box's own "Import report…" item (mRun(aceRepShow)) builds `` inside .acerep-read. That is the line-17795 sink, `'dollars in FY'+yrs[0]`, written unescaped. Chromium confirms it (inbrowser.mjs in the same folder): with that storage, opening the report sets window.__pw=2. The CSP has script-src 'unsafe-inline', so the planted handler runs. The code at 2bafb12 reads as described: `yrs` is R.years filtered only by `(R.total.v||{})[y]`, then concatenated raw at 17795 and into the year picker's option value and label at 17807. Every neighbour is escaped: R.sheet, R.row, the kept counts and ylbl. This breaks a rule the build was given, not a choice the builder recorded. The contract's "For every builder" section says "escape where drawn". CLAUDE.md v2.00 says a value that did not come from this board's own code is escaped where drawn, whatever the import check passed. notes-W1 records no decision to trust rep.years, and its hostile plants list the report's file, sheet, column titles, reasons, named rows and conflicts, but not the years. The proposed fix is sound. Number() turns the hostile string into NaN, and the integer filter drops it. Picks made in the box still match, since aceRepYrSet uses parseInt and MS.cur is a number. Escaping y in all three places also works.
votes.corrected: Reachability is stronger than the original evidence shows. The file passes the full-import door into a different board and survives the reopen. The menu's own Import report… item then puts the element on the page, and Chromium runs its onerror (window.__pw=2). The sink that is proven is line 17795 ('dollars in FY'+yrs[0], under .acerep-read). f.title: A deeper E-suffixed line folds back under the unsuffixed heading when a lower level's name matches, which is the fold the E rule exists to prevent
f.area: W1 import: the WBS tree, E-suffix rule
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceTree → walk (line 14899): `const h=(suf && bn && own && !aceNameSame(own, bn))? base+suf : base`, decided independently at each level
f.scenario: The ECU branch mirrors the plain one. Unsuffixed P6.2.2.1 has CES3 'Propulsion' and CES4 'Engine shop'. Suffixed P6.2.2.1.3E has CES3 'ECU Propulsion' and CES4 'Engine shop' (the same as the plain level-4 name). Level 3 differs and becomes P6.2.2E 'ECU Propulsion'. Level 4 matches and becomes the plain P6.2.2.1, whose parent is P6.2.2 'Propulsion'. The ECU leaf's path is 'Depot › CONUS › Propulsion › Engine shop › Tooling ECU', and P6.2.2E holds nothing. A requirement on P6.2.2E claims none of it; one on P6.2.2 claims it (aceLineUp follows aceWbsUp), so the AV/PSM split attributes it wrongly. The contract's per-level wording produces this too, so this is a gap in the contract as much as in the build.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p10-tree.mjs prints 'P6.2.2.1.3E {n:'Tooling ECU', lv:5, up:'P6.2.2.1'}', 'P6.2.2E {n:'ECU Propulsion', lv:3, up:'P6.2'}' and 'up of P6.2.2.1.3E: [[P6.2.2.1.3E, P6.2.2.1, P6.2.2, P6.2, P6], "Depot › CONUS › Propulsion › Engine shop › Tooling ECU"]'.
f.fix: In walk, once a level has taken the suffix (h!==base), give every heading below it on that line the suffix as well (base+suf), so the branch stays under its own suffixed heading. Add this 5-level mirrored fixture to the W1 block. Brad's examples (P6.2.2.1E, P6.5.1.2E) are unchanged by this.

votes.corrected: Confirmed as stated. Through the real import, a mirrored 5-level E line (P6.2.2.1.3E: CES3 'ECU Propulsion', CES4 equal to the plain P6.2.2.1's name) is filed under P6.2.2.1 → P6.2.2 'Propulsion', with no conflict and no named row. A requirement on P6.2.2E claims none of its dollars, and one on P6.2.2 claims them all. The contract's per-level wording allows this, but it defeats the purpose stated in item 132. The fix (suffix every heading below the first suffixed level) can collide with an existing suffixed leaf of the same code, such as P6.2.2.1E. When that leaf's name differs, a conflict is recorded.

votes.why:
I reproduced it with my own probe on the 2bafb12 board bytes (git show 2bafb12:prioritization-board-grid.html). The probe builds the workbook with the board's own buildXlsx and imports it through importAce, so it takes the real import path. It is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-3-1/probe.mjs, and it runs two cases.

**Control (Brad's examples): correct.** P6.2.2.1E sits under P6.2.2E 'ECU Propulsion', then P6.2. P6.5.1.2E sits under P6.5.1 'Government'.

**The finding's case: it folds.** The rows are plain P6.2.2.1.3 (CES3 'Propulsion', CES4 'Engine shop') and P6.2.2.1.3E (CES3 'ECU Propulsion', CES4 'Engine shop'). The probe printed:
- P6.2.2.1.3E {n:'Tooling ECU', lv:5, up:'P6.2.2.1'}
- P6.2.2E {n:'ECU Propulsion', lv:3, up:'P6.2'}, with no children
- aceLineUp(P6.2.2.1.3E) = [P6.2.2.1.3E, P6.2.2.1, P6.2.2, P6.2, P6], path 'Depot › CONUS › Propulsion › Engine shop › Tooling ECU'
- a requirement on P6.2.2 claims the ECU line; one on P6.2.2E claims nothing
- rep.conflicts is empty, so the import report says nothing about it

**Why the code does this.** In aceTree's walk, the suffix is decided level by level (`h=(suf&&bn&&own&&!aceNameSame(own,bn))?base+suf:base`). So level 4 takes the plain P6.2.2.1, and the walk passes up='P6.2.2E' for it. But put() keeps an existing node's up unchanged, so the parent the plain walk gave it (P6.2.2) silently stands.

**Is the 'should' grounded?** Yes, in what item 132 says the rule is for, though not in the contract's literal wording:
- The contract's per-level wording, and "A suffixed heading inherits the unsuffixed heading's parent", do produce this result, as the finding itself says.
- NEXT-VERSION.md item 132 states the rule's purpose: "done that way, the ECU lines fold under Propulsion", and "the location breakout under its own heading (P6.2.2E)".
- The builder's documented decision (notes-W1.md, and the comment above aceTree) is: "A suffixed heading's parent is the line's own heading one level up". Here that would make P6.2.2.1's parent P6.2.2E for this line, and the code drops it without saying so. That decision only explicitly covers two consecutive levels that differ; it does not cover this case.

So this is not a documented choice. It is a gap in the contract and the build together.

**Is it reachable?** Through a real ACE import, yes. A person needs a level-5 E line whose CES4 repeats its plain twin's name under a CES3 that differs. That is plausible for the location breakout Brad describes (mirrored sub-level names). But it is not a shape the recorded examples from Brad's file show: they are level-4 E lines only, which is why severity minor fits.
votes.corrected:
Same finding, with three corrections:
- The tree keeps the plain parent without naming a conflict: put() never replaces an existing node's up.
- This contradicts the builder's own stated rule that a suffixed line's heading takes "the line's own heading one level up" as its parent. It is not a documented decision.
- Reachability depends on a data shape (a level-5 E line with a matching CES4) that Brad's recorded examples do not show.

f.title: aceMoney reads figures out of words and loses signs, though its comment says 'a word reads as nothing, never as a figure'

f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceMoney (line 14813: `if(!isFinite(x)) x=parseFloat(s.replace(/[^0-9.\-]/g,''))`; the parentheses test runs only on a cell that starts with '(')

- '$(1.5)' → +1,500,000, while '($1.5)' and '(1.5)' → −1,500,000
- also '12/31/2026' → 12,312,026,000,000

Probe 2 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-4-0/p2-import.mjs) goes through the real door. The resulting lines are 1.1 {2027: 27,000,000}, 1.2 +1,500,000, 1.3 +1,500,000, 1.4 2,000,000 and 1.5 3,000,000, so the O&M FY27 total is $35,000,000. Only $2,000,000 of those cells are figures. Nothing is named: `rep.named` is empty. The status line says "No row left out. Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason" and reports the estimate locked.

Reachability: a person only needs to import a cost-estimate workbook where a year cell is text, such as one hand-edited or pasted as values. The build itself treats text money cells as real input. Its own audit-other fixture imports the year cell '(0.25)' as raw text, and v2.12 added the parentheses rule precisely for text cells. '$(1.5)' is the same accounting form the contract decided is negative, written with the $ outside.

Is it a decision? No. The contract (recovery/v212/contract.md line 95) and notes-W1.md line 40 say only: the cells are $M, (1.5) is −1.5, whole dollars at the door. Nothing decides that digits are pulled out of words.

Not a v2.12 regression: v2.11's import (f76e327, around line 14657) had the same `parseFloat` over stripped text. v2.12 rewrote the function and added a comment claiming the opposite. Severity minor is fair, since it needs a hand-made text cell.
votes.corrected:
Confirmed as stated. Three things to add.
- **Not new in v2.12.** v2.11's import ran the same `parseFloat` over text with everything but digits, points and hyphens stripped. What v2.12 adds is a comment on `aceMoney` claiming the opposite, while the code is unchanged in that respect.
- **The import report hides it.** A cell read this way is counted as a kept dollar and nothing is named. The status line then says "Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason".
- **A worse case.** A date typed as text, such as '12/31/2026', reads as $12,312,026 million.

'1,5' read as 15 follows from the comma-stripping the ACE import has always done. Other entry fields (`amtRead`) would refuse it, so treat that case as the weakest of the five.

votes.why:

The parentheses test is anchored at the start of the cell (`/^\((.*)\)$/`), so it runs only when the cell begins with '('. f.title: The file key no longer files a name where ACE touches the year ('2026ACE_final.xlsx', 'FY2026ACE.xlsx') under the estimate's key. A re-import makes a second estimate instead of asking to replace the locked one
f.area: W1 import: the file key
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html importAce, line 17623: `/(20\d\d)\b.*?\bACE\b/i`. The \b after the year fails when ACE (or any letter) follows it directly.
f.scenario: An estimate is already loaded and locked as 2026ACE. Each of '2026ACE_final.xlsx', '2026ACE Detail File.xlsx' and 'FY2026ACE.xlsx' is filed as its own key. The 'already loaded and LOCKED' question never appears, a second copy of the estimate is held, and spAce moves to it. 'FY2026ACE' gets aceYearOf 0, so wbsPickKey ranks it as the oldest. Under v2.11 all of these were 2026ACE. Only '2026ACE.xlsx' still works, by the fallback to the whole name.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p3-key.mjs prints 'estimates held after importing 6 files of one estimate: [["2026ACE",…],["2026ACE_final",…,2026],["2026ACE Detail File",…,2026],["FY2026ACE","FY2026ACE.xlsx",0]]', against the v2.11 keys 2026ACE ×4.
f.fix: Use `/(20\d\d)(?!\d).*?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i`: the year not followed by another digit, then ACE anywhere after it. This keeps '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE' working, restores the v2.11 names, and still refuses 'ACEs'.

votes.why:
I could not refute it. I read the code and wrote my own probe instead of using the reviewer's.

**The code.** At 2bafb12, importAce line 17623 reads `const label=(f.name.match(/(20\d\d)\b.*?\bACE\b/i)||[null,''])[1]`. The same line is still at 17674 on the integration HEAD, 6daac7d. From the board's first commit, 09cf071, up to d7ab715, the pattern was `/(20\d\d)\s*ACE/i`. If the label is empty, the key is the whole file name. aceImportGo asks the "already loaded and LOCKED" question only when `ACEDB.sets[key]` is already locked. A different key never asks: it adds a new locked set and moves spAce to it. aceYearOf reads `/^(20\d\d)/`, so a key such as 'FY2026ACE' gets year 0 and wbsPickKey ranks it oldest.

**Probe 1, the regex alone** (verify-w1-parse-5-0/regex.mjs). The v2.11 pattern keys '2026ACE_final.xlsx', '2026ACE Detail File.xlsx' and 'FY2026ACE.xlsx' as 2026ACE. The v2.12 pattern keys each under its whole name, because `\b` fails where the year touches ACE. A fourth name regressed that the finding missed: '2026 ACE_final.xlsx', because `\bACE\b` fails before '_'.

**Probe 2, the real importAce** (board.mjs). It boots the 2bafb12 bytes in jsdom, builds a real workbook with buildXlsx and counts every confirm() call. Steps:
- '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx' loaded as 2026ACE, locked.
- Each of '2026ACE_final.xlsx', 'FY2026ACE.xlsx' and '2026 ACE_final.xlsx' became its own locked set, with no question, and spAce moved to it each time. FY2026ACE got aceYearOf 0.
- The control, '2026 ACE approved.xlsx', did ask "2026ACE is already loaded and LOCKED".

**Is it reachable?** Yes. The file name is whatever the person picks in Data › Import Annual Cost Estimate. The original pattern's `\s*` was written to accept a year glued to ACE.

**Is the 'should' supported?** The contract and items 132/134 say nothing about the key. The builder's documented intent in notes-W1.md is "the year, then the word ACE anywhere after it", meant to widen the match for '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File'. The regex fails that stated intent for these names, so this is a side effect, not a documented decision. The board's own help (lines 4181 and 35156) also says an estimate "is keyed by its year (2025ACE) and locked on import, because an approved estimate should not change". 'FY2026ACE' is not keyed by its year.

**The proposed fix is wrong.** `/(20\d\d)(?!\d).*?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i` has no guard before ACE. It would file '2026 Workspace.xlsx', '2026 Interface Detail.xlsx' and '2026 TRACE.xlsx' as 2026ACE, so they would collide with the locked estimate (fix.mjs shows this). v2.11 and v2.12 both leave those names alone.
votes.corrected:
Use `/(?:^|\D)(20\d\d)(?!\d)(?:.*?[^A-Za-z])?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i` (capture group 1 is still the year, and there is no lookbehind, as the codebase prefers). Checked in fix.mjs:
- **Keyed 2026ACE:** '2026ACE.xlsx', '2026ACE_final.xlsx', '2026ACE Detail File.xlsx', 'FY2026ACE.xlsx', '2026 ACE_final.xlsx', '2026_ACE.xlsx', '2026-ACE.xlsx' and '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx'.
- **Unchanged:** '2027 ACE approved.xlsx' stays 2027ACE. The test template name '2025 ACE ${tag}.xlsx' stays 2025ACE.
- **Still refused:** '2026 ACEs', '2026 Workspace', '2026 Interface Detail', '2026 TRACE', '120265 ACE' and '20261 ACE'.

The finding also missed a regressed name: '2026 ACE_final.xlsx' is keyed under its whole name at 2bafb12, against 2026ACE under v2.11. A check of the fix should include a name where a word ending in "ace" follows the year (for example '2026 Workspace.xlsx'), so that a guard-less fix fails it.

votes.why:
I reproduced it with my own probe, built from scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-5-1/probe.mjs. The reviewer's probe answered every confirm() with OK, so it could not show whether the locked-estimate question was asked. Mine records each confirm() and answers Cancel.

**The code at 2bafb12.** importAce, line 17623, builds the label with `/(20\d\d)\b.*?\bACE\b/i`. Where nothing matches, the key falls back to the whole file name without `.xlsx`. aceImportGo asks the "already loaded and LOCKED" question only when `ACEDB.sets[key]` already exists. Otherwise it stores a new set and moves `spAce` and `MS.spAce` to it. v2.11 (main, line 15629) used `/(20\d\d)\s*ACE/i`.

**Probe result.** First, '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx' is imported, which gives 2026ACE, locked. Then each of these is imported with no question asked, each becomes its own estimate, and `spAce` moves to each in turn:
- '2026ACE_final.xlsx'
- '2026ACE Detail File.xlsx'
- 'FY2026ACE.xlsx' (its `aceYearOf` is 0)
- '2026 ACE_final.xlsx', a further case: ACE followed by '_' fails the second \b

v2.11 keys every one of these as 2026ACE, so it would have asked. Only '2026ACE.xlsx' (through the whole-name fallback) and '2026 ACE.xlsx' still reach the question.

**Reachable.** A person picks the file through the Data card's file input, so the key comes from the name on disk. Every import locks its estimate (`set.locked=true`), so the premise is a normal one.

**Not a documented decision.** notes-W1.md says the new pattern reads "the year, then the word ACE anywhere after it". It describes widening the old "year right before ACE" pattern. Nothing in notes-W1.md, contract.md or NEXT-VERSION.md item 132 says that names with the year right before ACE should stop being keyed. The \b after the year narrows the pattern, and nothing records that as intended.

**Severity: minor.** No figure is wrong and nothing is lost. The board holds an extra estimate and bypasses the locked-replace question.

**The proposed fix has its own defect.** `/(20\d\d)(?!\d).*?ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i` matches ACE at the end of any word. It would key '2026 SPACE plan.xlsx' and '2026 Interface.xlsx' as 2026ACE, and it would also match 'FACE', 'PLACE' and 'SURFACE'. I checked this in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-5-1/rx.mjs.
votes.corrected:
The finding stands, but its fix needs one change. Use `/(20\d\d)(?!\d)(?:|.*?[^A-Za-z])ACE(?![A-Za-z])/i`: the year not followed by a digit, then ACE either right after it or after a character that is not a letter, and ACE not followed by a letter. Checked in rx.mjs:
- It keys these as 2026ACE again, as v2.11 did: '2026ACE.xlsx', '2026ACE_final.xlsx', '2026ACE Detail File.xlsx', 'FY2026ACE.xlsx', '2026 ACE_final.xlsx'.
- It keeps '2026 SUST ACE COMPLETE Detail File.xlsx' and '2026-ACE.xlsx' as 2026ACE.
- It refuses '2026ACEs.xlsx', '2026 SPACE plan.xlsx' and '2026 Interface.xlsx'.

The finding's own regex keys the SPACE and Interface names as 2026ACE.

f.title: A second column headed by the same year is never read, and the report still says every dollar of the sheet ties
f.area: W1 import: fiscal-year columns, conservation claim
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceFindHeader, line 14863 `if(y && !(y in years)) years[y]=i`
f.scenario: The header carries 2027 twice, for example a second block of the same years. Only the first column is read. The $5,000,000 in the second 2027 column is in no total and no reason, and the report says '✓ Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in one reason above, every year, to the dollar.'
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p11-dup-year.mjs prints 'sheet total {"2027":1000000} kept {"2027":1000000} ties true', and the report text with the ✓ line.
f.fix: In aceFindHeader, record each year's columns. If a year heads more than one column, refuse the file and name the year and both column letters, or ask which to read. Never drop the column silently.

votes.why:
I read the code at 2bafb12 and wrote my own probe, which reproduces the finding. The probe loads the 2bafb12 board straight from git, builds the workbook with the board's own buildXlsx, and imports it through importAce, the same path as Data › Import Annual Cost Estimate.

**The code.** aceFindHeader (2bafb12 line 14863, unchanged at HEAD 6daac7d line 14914) has `if(y && !(y in years)) years[y]=i`, so only the first column headed by each year is kept. aceParse builds each row's `vec` from `ycol[y]` only. `rep.total.v` is summed from that same `vec`, so a second column headed by the same year is in no total and no reason, and `rep.ties` still comes out true. The report does not list which column each year was read from, so nothing on screen shows the drop.

**The probe:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-8-0/probe-dup-year.mjs`
- **A second 2027 column holding $5M:** the sheet total and kept both read 2027 = 2,500,000, and the $5M is in neither. `ties` is true. The status line says "Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason", and the report shows "✓ Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in one reason above, every year, to the dollar."
- **A second block 2026/2027/2028 holding $7M, $8M and $9M:** all $24M dropped, with the same ✓ line.
- **' 2027 ' as padded text:** dropped the same way.
- **Control, no duplicate:** identical figures, so the extra column changed nothing at all.

**Reachable:** yes, through the board's own import control, by a file whose header carries a year twice. Brad's real 2026 file has one column per year (NEXT-VERSION.md item 132), so it needs a changed or hand-edited file. Brad said ACE files "sometimes change and add new columns", and that is why the import reads by title.

**The 'should' comes from the contract.** It reads "the fiscal years (every header that is a year 1991–2099)", "nothing is guessed" and "nothing is read by position". First column wins is a positional choice, made silently.

**Not a documented decision.** notes-W1.md says nothing about a repeated year. Its "ties holds by construction" gap is about mutation coverage; it does not excuse a ✓ claim that is false for the sheet. W3 does not touch this code.

Severity minor is fair.
votes.corrected: Confirmed as stated. It needs a workbook whose header names one year in two columns. Brad's real 2026 file has one column per year, so this is a changed or hand-edited file, which item 132 explicitly expects the import to survive. The same first-wins rule (`at[n]`) applies to a repeated field title; that is a separate finding.

votes.why:
The code at 2bafb12 does what the finding says. In prioritization-board-grid.html, aceFindHeader line 14863 is `hdr.forEach(function(c, i){ const y=aceYearOfHdr(c); if(y && !(y in years)) years[y]=i; });`, so each year keeps only its first column. aceParse builds every row's `vec`, and so `rep.total`, only from `ycol[y]`. A second column under the same year is therefore in no total and no reason. `rep.ties` (line 15007) can only compare what was read against itself.

I wrote my own probe instead of using the reviewer's lib: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-8-1/probe.mjs. It builds the workbook with buildXlsx and imports it through the real importAce path. Results:
- A (2026, 2027, 2028, 2027; $1M then $5M): total and kept are both {2027: 1,000,000} and ties is true. The report reads "✓ Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in one reason above, every year, to the dollar." The status line says "No row left out. Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason." The $5M is silently gone.
- B (the same with the years as text): the same result.
- C (the other block placed first): the first column by position is read, here $5M where the board's block holds $1M, still with ✓.
- D (one 2027 column, the control): identical to A, so nothing on screen tells A from a clean file.

The report's "Columns read, by title" table lists only ACE_FIELDS. It never shows which column a year came from.

I found no decision covering this. Neither notes-W1.md nor notes-W3.md says anything about a year heading more than one column. The contract reads the fiscal years as "every header that is a year 1991–2099". Item 132 in NEXT-VERSION.md records Brad's rule: "nothing is guessed and nothing is read by position". Taking the first of two same-year columns is exactly a choice by position.

How a person meets it: through Data › Import Annual Cost Estimate, on a file whose layout has changed. Brad said "the ACE files sometimes change and add new columns". The 2026 file Brad described has one column per year, so the case is not in today's file, which makes "minor" fair. It is still reachable on a file the board is built to accept, and it ends in silent dollar loss under an affirmative ✓.
votes.corrected: The finding stands, and variant C makes it a little worse. Because the first column by position wins, a repeated year block placed BEFORE the real dollars is the one read: those figures are kept as the estimate, with the same ✓, while the real dollars are dropped. The fix should treat both orders alike. When a year heads more than one column, refuse the file (or ask which column to read), naming the year and every column letter (aceColL). Neither copy should be silently preferred.

f.title: The import report trusts any rep that has `reasons`. One without `kept` or `total` makes aceRepBody throw inside render(), and nothing after it in render() draws while the report is open
f.area: W1 import report: robustness on a damaged file
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html aceRepBody, line 17781 (`if(!R || typeof R!=='object' || !R.reasons)`), then unguarded reads of R.kept.lines, R.total.v and R.absent.map
f.scenario: A hand-made or damaged board file carries rep:{v:1, reasons:{}, named:[], conflicts:[]}. It passes the import check. The person opens Data › Import report… and render() stops at aceRepBody, so syncBtns, the menus and every panel after it are not redrawn until the report is closed. This is the class v2.07 fixed in budRegBody and spBodyDraw.
f.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w1import/p9-rep-throws.mjs prints 'passes the import check: passes' and 'render with the report open: threw: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'lines')'.
f.fix: Treat the report as old unless R.kept, R.total and R.reasons are objects and R.named, R.absent and R.conflicts are arrays, and say so in the acerep-old hint. Or default each of them (`const K=R.kept&&typeof R.kept==='object'? R.kept : {}`, and so on).

votes.why:
I could not refute this one, and my own probe reproduced it on the 2bafb12 board (extracted to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-9-0/board-2bafb12.html, probe p1.mjs in the same folder).

The code, read at 2bafb12:
- aceRepBody (line 17767) only falls back to the "imported before v2.12" hint when R has no `reasons`.
- It then reads `R.total.v`, `R.kept.lines` and `R.kept.rows` with no guard.
- render() calls aceRepBody inline at line 30042. The wrapper at 37564 is `try{ renderBoard.apply(...) } finally{...}` with no catch, so the throw leaves render(). The rest of the board body, syncBtns, gridAfterRender, focusRestore, fitMenus and dlgSync all go unrun.

The door lets the file through:
- inShapeWhy has no rule for an ACE set's `rep`.

f.title: A tagged board whose position has a line list that is not a list no longer opens, and importing it half-lands while saying it failed
f.area: W3 live budget authority: boot first pass, applyStore, baOf
f.where: baOf -> ppSvcFy -> ppKeysOf (`((P.lines||{})[sv]||[]).forEach`), reached from applyBudget inside applyState inside applyStore. applyBudget has no try/catch.
f.scenario: A board file (hand-edited, damaged, or written by another build) is tagged BES28, and its BES28 position has `lines.USAF` as a string, number or plain object, or holds a null entry, while `val.USAF` has a figure. In v2.11 the file opens normally: positions were read only when the PPBE box or the Spruills opened. In v2.12, opening it runs the budget read during the top-level applyStore. That throws 'Uncaught TypeError: ((P.lines || {})[sv] || []).forEach is not a function', the script stops, and no requirement is drawn. The import door passes the file (inboundCheck returns ''). If the same store comes in through importState's JSON path, applyStore has already replaced MS when the error is thrown. The person is told 'Could not read that file.', but the board now holds the file's store, half applied (its bm and order are on screen), and the next Save writes that store over the board.
f.evidence: Probes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w3ba/p10.mjs printed 'v2.11 opens it: requirements 3 errors []' and 'v2.12 opens it: ... errors [Uncaught [TypeError: ((P.lines || {})[sv] || []).forEach is not a function]]', 'row count on screen 0', 'door says: ""'. p11.mjs printed: board before bm.disc [1000,400,300]; after the failed import {"said":"alert: Could not read that file. (...)","nowBm":[1,2,3],"nowOrder":["C","B","A"],"msCycle":"BES|2028"}.
f.fix: Smallest fix: in ppKeysOf, read the list as `const L=(P.lines||{})[sv]; (Array.isArray(L)? L : []).forEach(l=>{ if(l && typeof l==='object' && !seen[l.k]) ...})`. Also make baOf degrade rather than throw: wrap each service's ppSvcFy read in try/catch, keep the board's own base for that service and mark it 'board'. Optionally have the door refuse a position whose `lines[svc]` is not a list of objects.

- v2.12 opens every variant with 0 rows and an uncaught `TypeError` (forEach is not a function, or reading 'k' of null).
- `inboundCheck` returns '' for all four, and nothing at the door looks at ppbe shapes.

q2 runs the real `importState` on a populated board (IS_SHELL is false once a saved board with a data pack is booted). The file is a JSON state with the same position, its own `bm` [1,2,3] and its own order C,B,A.

1. **The trigger is narrow.** No ORBIT build writes a `lines[svc]` that is not a list of objects: `ppLines`, `ppNorm`, `ppLineAdd` and `ppLineDel` (which uses filter) always keep a real array. So "written by another build" does not happen in practice. The real trigger is a hand-edited or foreign file, which CLAUDE.md does treat as input the board meets. On that basis, moderate fits the severity better than major.
2. **A blank board is the file path only.** When the board reopens from browser storage, the storage restore is inside a try/catch (q3). It opens, showing 3 rows and setting `_bootRestoreErr`, with a half-applied store rather than a blank board.

2. After that failed import:

5. Shapes that throw: `lines[svc]` as a string, number or plain object, or a list holding a null entry. A whole `lines` field that is a string does not throw.
6. Fix: guard `ppKeysOf` the way `codeIssues` already guards the same container, with `Array.isArray(L)` and a skip for any entry that is not an object. Optionally also make `baOf` degrade per service.

f.title: Viewing a v2.12 lock taken while the plan's tag logged no position says it was locked before v2.12 and that the plan was untagged
f.area: W3: cycLock's c.pos, baPos, fitBody/fitSrcSay
f.where: cycLock stores `pos:null` when the tag logs no position for this appropriation, so baPos() in the view returns null, the same as for a pre-v2.12 lock. fitBody's hint then takes the `CYCVIEW && !M.lock` branch, and fitSrcSay takes the `!r.key` branch.
f.scenario: Tag the plan POM28 (no POM28 position on this board) and lock POM28 in v2.12. Open the lock's view and the fit box. It says 'Viewing O&M POM28 (locked): it was locked before v2.12 and kept no position', and each year says 'The plan is untagged: every base is the board’s own'. The lock was taken in this build, while the plan was tagged POM28.
f.evidence: Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w3ba/p2.mjs printed 'lock pos null' and both quoted texts.
f.fix: Store `pos:{key:posNow.key, P:null}` (or `pos:null, posV:1`) when the tag logs nothing, so a v2.12 lock can be told from a pre-v2.12 one. baPos then returns {key, P:null, lock}. Reword the view's hint and fitSrcSay to say '<key> logged no position for <appropriation> when this was locked'.

- In a view, baPos (26856) returns null unless `c.pos.P` is an object.
- So fitModel's M.key and M.lock are both ''.
- fitBody then takes the `CYCVIEW && !M.lock` branch: "it was locked before v2.12 and kept no position".
- fitSrcSay takes `!r.key`: "The plan is untagged: every base is the board’s own".

A person reaches this with the board's own controls: the PPBE cycles panel's tag select/year (cycSetWorking) and its 🔒 Lock button (cycLock).

What the probe found:
- **S1, the commonest case.** A fresh untagged board with no PPBE position locks PB27. The plan is tagged PB|2027 after the lock, and the lock HAS a `pos` field, set to null. - **Control A.** A BES28 lock shows "its years read the BES28 position as it was when it was locked" and "Base from BES28 for USAF…".

f.title: The over sentence says requirements hold '$X more than BES28' when $X is measured against BES28 plus added funding
f.area: W3: fitBody's over sentence
f.where: fitBody: `vs=r.from[i]==='pos'? key : 'its budget authority'`, printed with `X.over[i]`, where over = held minus BA, and BA includes the lane's added sources.
f.scenario: FY27 USAF discretionary: BES28 900, Cong add 150, BA 1,050, held 1,100. The box says '▲ FY27 O&M, USAF discretionary: requirements hold $50 more than BES28 — reduce a requirement'. Requirements actually hold $200 more than BES28's $900. The $50 is past BES28 plus the add. Someone checking the figure against the position finds it does not add up.
f.evidence: Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w3ba/p12.mjs printed that sentence and 'FY27 USAF disc: BES28 900 added 150 BA 1050 held 1100'.
f.fix: When X.add[i] is not zero, word it against the budget authority. For example: 'requirements hold $50 more than the budget authority (BES28 $900 + $150 added)'.

It used Budget Management's + Add funding source (bmAddSrc) and its box (bmSrcSet), the PPBE Budget Positions cell (ppSetV, BES28 USAF FY27 d 900), the retag (cycSetWorking('BES',2028)) and a typed Split (setFsrcSvc A USAF d 1100).

A negative source (a withhold, which bmSrcSet accepts with {neg:true}) makes it worse. With add -150 and held 800, BA is 750 and the box still says "requirements hold $50 more than BES28", though they hold $100 LESS than BES28.

The scenario is reachable. Budget Management still offers Add funding source on a tagged plan, and added sources beside the position are Brad's own decision 4 in item 134. The cause is in fitBody: vs=key whenever r.from[i]==='pos', while X.over = held − BA, and BA = base + adds (fitYearNow, baOf).

The best case for refuting it is that contract.md gives this sentence verbatim beside over = max(0, held − BA). notes-W3 says the builder used it "as Brad worded it", so the builder did not stray from the contract. But the contract's own BA includes added sources. Neither the contract nor notes-W3 records a decision about how to word the sentence when a lane has an added source. So the template is only true when added is 0, and the printed figure and its comparison disagree. This is the kind of naming of the wrong limit that CLAUDE.md ("Two limits refuse a dollar, and they are not the same sentence") treats as a defect. f.area: W3 live budget: baApplyTo / baLiveAll at opening
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html baApplyTo() line 26913, which calls baOf() line 26872. `const d=bm.disc.slice()` and `t[i]+=(v||0)` (line 26887) read a year that applyState() has not yet normalised. f.scenario: A saved board's FY28 (not the year on screen) holds its budget the way an older file or a hand edit writes it: bm.disc ['1,100','410','310'] and a Cong add vec ['75','0','0']. The import check accepts this, because amounts may be text the board reads as figures, and applyState() heals it whenever the year is opened. The person opens the file in v2.12 with FY27 on screen, makes any edit and saves. On opening, FY28's stored cache became [0, 4100, 3100]: '1,100'+75 is NaN, so 0; '410'+'0' is '4100'. The saved file carries those figures. A base saved with fractions ([333.33, 333.33, 333.34], from before v1.97) is rounded service by service to [333,333,333], total 999. applyState apportions it to [333,333,334], total 1000. On the slot commit the stored cache stays as the file had it, [1175,410,310]. Anything that reads the stored cache, such as another appropriation's Spruills from this board's saved file, gets the wrong budget.
f.evidence: Probes in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/w3fit/. p3-text-amounts.mjs: 'the door on that file: (accepted)'; 'FY28 stored budget cache on opening (FY27 on screen): [[0,4100,3100],[210,110,60]]'; 'FY28 in the fit (worked on a copy): [1175,410,310]'; 'FY28 once opened (applyState heals the text): [[1175,410,310],...]'. p3b-text-amounts-saved.mjs: 'opened in v2.12, FY27 edited and saved -- FY28 cache in the saved file: [0,4100,3100]'. The same probe with BOARD set to the slot commit's board (slot-board.html, from git show d732259) prints '[1175,410,310]'. p3c-fraction.mjs: 'FY28 stored disc cache on opening: [333,333,333] total 999' against 'FY28 once opened: [333,333,334] total 1000'.
f.fix: In baApplyTo, leave a year for applyState unless every entry of bm.disc, bm.mand and each adds[].vec is a finite whole number. Extend the `w()` guard, as width is already handled. Better still, read the components through applyState's own rules (money() and bmTot, factored out once) so the two cannot differ. Add a check that opens a file with text and fractional components in an unopened year and compares its stored cache to the year opened.

The code does what the finding says, but only on a crafted file. For every file a real ORBIT build wrote, it changes nothing.

My probe a-text.mjs built a board with numbers and saved it. I then hand-edited FY28 in pubState to bm.disc ['1,100','410','310'] and the add's vec ['75','0','0']. The import check accepts that file. Opened on 2bafb12 with FY27 on screen, FY28's cache read [[0,4100,3100],[210,110,60]], and an FY27 edit followed by Save wrote that cache into the file. The same pubState on the slot board (d732259) kept [1175,410,310]. So the mechanics are reproduced.

2. **No real file reaches it.** Every writer of budget components turns its input into a number, in 2bafb12 and back to the first committed board (09cf071): bmSetBase and bmSrcSet go through parseAmt, svcRemapState permutes what is there, bmSeedFromPp uses D$, and applyState heals on load. No ORBIT build ever saved text into bm, so the "older file" in the scenario does not exist. Text there comes only from a hand edit of the JSON inside the HTML.

3. **The fraction claim fails on a real file.** p3c planted a cache of [333,333,334] that no build writes. My probe b-fraction-v196.mjs made the file with the v1.96 board itself: setBATot('disc','1000') in FY28, back to FY27, Save. v1.96 stored bm.disc [333.33…] with the cache [333,333,333], because its applyBudget already rounded each service with D$. Opened on 2bafb12, the FY28 cache is [333,333,333] on opening and after Save. The slot board gives exactly the same, and FY28 opened reads [334,333,333] on both. baApplyTo does the same arithmetic as the old applyBudget on the same raw parts, so for any year a build wrote, it reproduces the cache that build stored. The only exception is a year written before v1.59 and not opened in any later build: there the cache moves from fractions summing to 1,000 to whole dollars summing to 999. That is $1, in a figure printed in $M.

4. **Reach of the wrong cache.** The board's own Spruills calls spOwnYear, which runs aceWithYear and heals the stored year in place before reading it: it printed 2275, and the cache read [1175,410,310] afterwards. The fit works on a copy, and opening the year heals it too. Only another appropriation's Spruills block, and the live-view headline for a peer's year on screen, read a stored cache raw.

- Only another appropriation's Spruills block, and the live-view headline for a peer's year on screen, read that stored cache raw.

f.title: A year started by Copy to year or Roll forward keeps the blank year's $0 budget cache, and Save writes it into the file
f.area: W3 (item 134): every year's cache made live
f.where: yearCopy (`if(!MS.years[y]) MS.years[y]=freshYearState()`) and the Roll forward that uses it. Nothing calls baLiveAll or baApplyTo for the new year, and fitModel reads other years on a copy (fitReadYear), so the stored cache is never refreshed.
f.scenario: The plan is tagged BES28, and BES28 logs USAF FY30 at $777 / $33. The person copies a requirement into FY30, which does not exist yet, and saves.
f.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/complete/p5-yearcopy-cache.mjs: the stored FY30 cache after save is [[0,0,0],[0,0,0]], FY30 as the fit reads it is [[777,0,0],[33,0,0]], and FY30 in the saved file is [[0,0,0],[0,0,0]]. f.fix: When yearCopy creates a year, call baApplyTo(MS.years[y], y). Alternatively, call baLiveAll() in save() before persisting; it does no applyState and is cheap.

Reachability: a person meets this easily. Positions are optional, and any appropriation that logs nothing under the tag hits it. The box is meant to be used in a view; the W3 lock block opens it there.

The contract allows `pos` null and says the budget reads as locked. The money is right. The contract does not word the box. notes-W3 lists four cases (working tag, a lock's copy, a lock before v2.12, untagged) and never decides this fifth one, so it is an oversight, not a documented decision.

More evidence of intent: fitSrcSay has a sentence for exactly this case: `if(!r.has) return (r.lock? 'This lock kept no '+key+' position for '+appn …`. It can never run. r.lock is set only in baPos's view branch, and that branch requires P, which makes r.has true.

Severity: minor is right. Two sentences are false; no figure is wrong.
votes.corrected: The finding stands, with one correction to its first suggested fix. A test like `hasOwnProperty(c,'pos')` would tell the cases apart. But the wording it proposes, "PB27 logged no O&M position", is wrong when the plan was tagged under another cycle: a plan tagged BES28 and locked as PB27 read the BES28 position, and `pos:null` has lost that key. The alternative is the accurate fix. Store `pos:{key:posNow.key, P:null}`, and let baPos's CYCVIEW branch return `{key, P:null, lock}` for it. That makes fitSrcSay's existing, currently unreachable sentence ("This lock kept no BES28 position for O&M") the year line. fitBody's hint would then need a branch for a lock that has a key and no P.

f.title: An estimate with a partial stored import report makes every redraw throw while Data › Import report… is open
f.area: W1 (item 132): the report box
f.where: aceRepBody: it guards only `R.reasons`, then reads `R.total.v`, `R.kept.lines`, `R.kept.zero` and `R.kept.v` unguarded. It is called from the render() panel list, and the import check does not look at rep's shape.
f.scenario: A board holds an estimate whose rep has reasons but no total or kept (a hand-edited or cut-short file; the saved board passes the door). The person opens the import report.
f.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/complete/p6-rep-damaged.mjs: "door on the saved board: (passes the door)", "open the report: render threw: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'v')", and "any later render while it is open: next render threw". The rows stop redrawing until the box is closed. This is the class the v2.07 review fixed in budRegBody and spBodyDraw.
f.fix: Read `const K=R.kept||{}, TT=R.total||{}` (and `K.v||{}`, `TT.v||{}`), or treat a rep without kept and total as the older-report case.

votes.why:
I reproduced it at 2bafb12 with my own probe, which goes through a real file and the board's own controls (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-contract-7-0/probe.mjs).

How the probe ran:
- It seeded a board and put a well-formed 2026 estimate on it (tools/ace-seed.mjs ACE_REP_SEED). As a control, that estimate's report opens with 5,578 characters drawn.
- It saved the board with buildSavedHtml() and hand-edited the pubState JSON to delete rep.kept and rep.total, keeping rep.reasons.
- inboundCheck() on the edited file returns '' (it passes the door), so a full import would take it as well as opening it directly. Opened directly, it booted with no errors and the estimate loaded.
- It then clicked the Data card's real 'Import report…' button (mRun(aceRepShow), run after its setTimeout).

Results:
- The click threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'v')".
- #aceRepPanel became 'modal-bg open' with an empty body (0 chars), so the box opened blank with nothing said.
- With the box open, clicking requirement B's row ★ set S.mc.B=true, but its render() threw at the same place. The row still showed aria-pressed=false, so the rows really stop redrawing, and every direct render() threw too.
- The box's own close control (aceRepClose) put everything back: render() succeeded and the star showed.

The code agrees. aceRepBody (line 17767) guards only `!R.reasons` (the pre-v2.12 case), then reads `(R.total.v||{})` and `R.kept.lines/zero/rows/v` unguarded. It is called from render()'s panel list ahead of the rows. The render wrapper is try/finally, so the throw propagates.

Is the 'should' a real requirement? No decision in notes-W1.md or the contract excuses a partial report. CLAUDE.md's house style is that errors degrade rather than throw. v2.07 fixed this same class, found by the hostile sweep: budRegBody and spBodyDraw 'each stopped every redraw while their panel was open'. W1's own Data-card line for the same item is guarded (`(R.kept||{}).lines||0`), and it rendered '0 lines kept' for this estimate, so the builder anticipated a partial report in one place and not in the other.

Two weaknesses, neither enough to refute:
- The only route is a hand-edited or otherwise damaged file. A board file or folder copy works, since aceIntact's fingerprint does not cover rep. A 'cut-short' file would fail to parse as JSON, so that part of the scenario does not hold.
- The board recovers once the box is closed.

'minor' is the right severity.
votes.corrected: The scenario is reachable only through a hand-edited (or otherwise damaged but still parseable) saved board or folder estimate copy, not a cut-short one, which would fail to parse. Opening Data › Import report… on such an estimate shows an empty box with no message, and every render() throws while it is open: the rows do not redraw, for example a ★ toggled on a row stays unpressed on screen though S.mc changes. Closing the box restores the board. The Data card's own line for the item is already guarded (`(R.kept||{}).lines||0`). Fix as proposed: read `const K=R.kept||{}, TT=R.total||{}` (and `K.v||{}`, `TT.v||{}`), or treat a report without kept and total as the older-report case.

votes.why:
I reproduced it at 2bafb12 (prioritization-board-grid.html), on the path a real file takes, not only in memory.

**What the code does.** `aceRepBody()` (line 17767) has one guard: `!R || typeof R!=='object' || !R.reasons`. Past that guard it reads `(R.total.v||{})`, `R.kept.lines`, `R.kept.zero`, `R.kept.rows`, `R.kept.v`, `R.total.rows` and `R.total.v` without checking any of them. It is called from the panel list in `render()` at line 30042. That list runs before the rows are drawn, and the wrapper around `renderBoard` (line 37564) has a try/finally with no catch, so the throw ends the whole redraw. Nothing between the file and the box checks or repairs `rep`:
- ACEDB's boot pick (line 3049) takes the file's `aceDb` as it is.
- `importStores` copies a set across whole.
- `aceFingerprint` covers only `appn` and the line count.
- The import check passes the file.

The Data card's menu line already reads `(R.kept||{})` (line 30733), but the box does not.

**My probe** is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-contract-7-1/probe.mjs`. It saves a board holding an estimate whose `rep` is `{v:1, reasons:{}, years:[2027]}`, reopens that saved file in a fresh browser, and opens the report as the Data card does (`aceRepShow()` with no argument). Results:
- The import check passes the file.
- The reopened board holds the `rep` keys as saved.
- `syncBtns` is fine.
- Opening the report throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'v')". The box is open and empty.
- After a rename, the next `render()` throws the same way, and row A does not show the new title.
- After `aceRepClose()` the board redraws and row A shows the new title.

A `rep` with `kept` but no `total` throws the same way. The controls pass: a complete `rep`, and no `rep` at all (the older-report case), both draw and keep redrawing.

**Is it reachable?** The board's own import (line 14919) always writes a whole `rep`. So the only way in is a saved file that was hand-edited or crafted. A file cut short would not parse at all, so that half of the finding's scenario is not realistic. Even so, this is the class the project counts as a defect:
- CLAUDE.md v1.88: a file from someone else is data.
- CLAUDE.md v2.07: the hostile sweep's "an estimate with no totals (spBodyDraw)" and the BAE entry in `budRegBody` "each stopped every redraw while their panel was open", and both were fixed.

Neither notes-W1.md nor the contract records a decision to accept this. The effect is bounded: the static ✕ Close, a click on the backdrop and Esc all restore the board. Minor is the right severity, and the suggested fix (read `R.kept||{}` and `R.total||{}`, or treat a `rep` without them as the older report) fits.

f.title: The new guide sections claim more than the code does
f.area: Guide (helpDoc t-ppbe, t-ace)
f.where: <template id="helpDoc">: t-ppbe paragraph 2, t-ace paragraphs 1 and 3.
f.scenario: A person reads Help to learn what the board guarantees.
f.evidence: (1) t-ppbe says "Funded is still what the lane draws, so no report states more than the position." With added funding, or a service the position does not name, funded is above the position: in p2-over-adds.mjs, USAF FY27 discretionary drew $1,050 against BES28's $900. (2) t-ace says "If a title has changed, a box lists the file's own headers and asks which holds that field — once". Only required fields are asked; a renamed US/PTN/FMS is silently read as US (p3-partner-renamed.mjs above). (3) t-ace says the report shows "every named row". aceRepBody shows the first ACE_REP_CAP (40) of each kind, and the rest are only in the saved record, which no screen shows. Probe paths: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/complete/p2-over-adds.mjs and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/complete/p3-partner-renamed.mjs.
f.fix: (1) Say "no report states more than the budget authority (the position plus added funding)". (2) Say "a required column whose title changed is asked about", or ask about the optional ones too (see the US/PTN/FMS finding). (3) Say "the first 40 of each kind are shown", or make the rest reachable from the report.

votes.why:
I read the board at 2bafb12 (helpDoc lines 2312-2321, ACE_FIELDS, aceFindHeader, aceColDraw, aceRepBody) and wrote three probes of my own. All three over-claims hold.

(1) t-ppbe says "Funded is still what the lane draws, so no report states more than the position." Probe q1-funded-vs-position.mjs: a plan tagged BES28, BES28 FY27 USAF discretionary at 900, a Cong add of 150 on USAF discretionary, and requirement A asking 1,200. tiers() gives A d=[1050,0,0] and fitModel gives base 900, add 150, BA 1050, drawn 1050. So funded is $150 above the position. A person reaches this with ordinary controls: tag the plan and keep an added funding source in Budget Management. The code is right: item 134 decision 4 counts added funding beside the position. The sentence is wrong. It copies item 134's 'Proposed' line word for word, and that line is itself loose given decision 4. The code is not at fault.

(2) t-ace says "If a title has changed, a box lists the file's own headers and asks which holds that field — once". aceFindHeader only puts a field in `need` when it is required (`if(F.req) need.push(F.f)`). The contract and notes-W1 both scope the box to required fields. Probe q2-renamed-titles.mjs:
- Service renamed to Svc opens the box with need=['svc'] (the control case).
- US/PTN/FMS renamed to "Customer" opens no box. The PTN and FMS rows are kept as US: 3 lines, $6,000,000 instead of 1 line and $1,000,000, and partner rows = 0.
- CES3 renamed opens no box, and paragraph 1.1.1's name comes out blank.

CES2-CES8 are in the guide's own list of titles, so the over-claim is not only about US/PTN/FMS. One nuance: "silently" goes slightly too far. The report has a collapsed "Columns read" section that says "Not in this file (they name nothing): … US/PTN/FMS". No box asks, though.

(3) t-ace says the report shows "every named row". Probe q3-named-cap.mjs: 45 rows under an unknown PMO. The record holds 45, the report shows 40, and its hint reads "The first 40 of 45 are shown; the import keeps every one with the estimate." Nothing else reads rep.named: there is no export and no other screen. The contract's own wording is "capped on screen, whole in the record", and the guide dropped the cap.

All three are wording defects in the guide only. Severity minor, as the finding says. Probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-contract-8-0/ (q1-funded-vs-position.mjs, q2-renamed-titles.mjs, q3-named-cap.mjs), and each runs against board.html extracted there from 2bafb12.
votes.corrected: Confirmed, with two refinements. (1) The t-ppbe sentence is copied word for word from item 134's 'Proposed' text. The code is right to count added funding (decision 4), so only the guide needs rewording, to "no report states more than the budget authority (the position plus added funding)". Item 134's own line has the same looseness. (2) A renamed optional column is not entirely silent: the report's collapsed "Columns read" section lists it under "Not in this file". But no box asks, and that covers CES2-CES8 (which the guide lists) as well as US/PTN/FMS and the CCAR columns. The guide should say "a required column whose title changed is asked about". (3) The report shows the first 40 of each kind and says so on screen; nothing shows the rest. The guide's "every named row" should say "the first 40 of each kind on screen, every one kept with the estimate".

votes.why:
I checked all three claims against the code at 2bafb12 (/home/user/orbit-board) and with my own probes in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-contract-8-1/. All three hold. Each is a person reading Help next to what the board does.

(1) t-ppbe paragraph 2 says "Funded is still what the lane draws, so no report states more than the position." So Funded on screen is above the position. This is the design: Brad's decision 4 on item 134 counts added sources beside the position, and the same guide section says "added funding sources still add on top". The sentence is word for word from item 134's "Proposed" text in NEXT-VERSION.md. That text was already loose once decision 4 applies, so being in the log does not make the guide accurate.

(2) t-ace paragraph 1 says "If a title has changed, a box lists the file's own headers and asks which holds that field — once … A field still unanswered refuses the file". In the code, `aceFindHeader` puts a field in `need` only `if(F.req)`, and only `need` opens `#aceColPanel`. The contract agrees: "A required field the file does not title is asked for once". Probe v2-renamed-title.mjs:
- T/M/S renamed: the box opens, asking for ['tms'] (control).
- CES2 renamed: no box and no refusal. CES2 is a title the guide itself lists under "CES1–CES8"; the file just imports with ces2 among the absent fields.
- US/PTN/FMS renamed: no box. The PTN and FMS rows are kept as US money (3 lines, $6,000,000 kept against $1,000,000 in the control, 0 partner rows), and the status line says "No row left out".

(3) t-ace paragraph 3 says the report shows "every named row". `aceRepBody` draws `L.slice(0, ACE_REP_CAP)` with ACE_REP_CAP=40. Probe v3-named-cap.mjs: 45 rows under an unknown office are stored in `rep.named`, the report draws 40, and WBS 1.46 appears nowhere on the page. The contract says "capped on screen, whole in the record", so the cap is meant; the guide just leaves it out.

The builder notes (notes-W1.md, notes-W3.md) record no decision to word the guide this way. Minor severity is right: the code matches the contract in each case and only the guide text overstates it.
votes.corrected:
Confirmed as stated, with three refinements:
- (1) The guide repeats item 134's "Proposed" sentence word for word. It is still false whenever an added funding source is drawn (Brad's decision 4).
- (2) Titles the guide itself lists, CES2–CES8, are not asked about either. US/PTN/FMS is not in the guide's list, but its "partner or FMS lines" sentence depends on that column.
- (3) The report's own hint says "The first 40 of N are shown; the import keeps every one with the estimate". Only the guide's "every named row" overstates it; the rest are in the saved record, which no screen shows.

Fix as the finding proposes: "budget authority (the position plus added funding)"; "a required column whose title changed is asked about"; "the first 40 of each kind are shown".

f.title: The W3 fit checks cannot tell a Split's typed figure from the clamped one, though the money map says they prove it
f.area: W3 checks (audit-board 'v2.12 W3 — the fit to the position…', w3Board fixture; tools/money-map.json w3.fit)
f.where: tools/export-audit/audit-board.mjs w3Board() and the fit block; prioritization-board-grid.html fitYearNow() (`const v=fsDirVec(it) || {d:p.d, m:p.m};`); tools/money-map.json 'w3.fit'
f.scenario: An office reduces a requirement's value below the Split already typed against it, which is the ordinary way to 'reduce a requirement' and fit BES28. On the shipped board the fit reads the Split clamped to the new value: held drops and the over clears. If fitYearNow read the typed Split directly (no clamp), the over would stay and Needs attention would keep saying '🏛 1 over' after the person has reduced the requirement. Nothing would fail. Every Split in w3Board is typed to exactly its requirement's value (A dv+mv = [600,200,100] = ask; B = [500,300,200] = ask), so the clamped and unclamped readings agree. Yet money-map w3.fit lists 'held (Splits’ typed figures clamped to the basis …)' as proven. No mutation targets the clamp.
f.evidence: Variant /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/variants/held-unclamped.html makes fitYearNow read S.fsrc[id].dv/mv raw. All three W3 blocks (slimmed copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/checks/export-audit/_slim-w3all.mjs) print ALL CHECKS PASSED. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/checks/probes/held-clamp.mjs: USAF, A ask 600, Split 600, BA 550, then setAsk('A',0,'500'). Shipped: before [held 600, drawn 550, over 50], after [500, 500, over 0, unallocated 50], Needs attention none. Variant: after [600, 500, over 50, 0], Needs attention '🏛 1 over budget authority'.
f.fix: In w3Board, type one Split above its requirement's value, or lower the value after the Split with setAsk (e.g. A's USAF Split 650 on a 600 value). Then assert held, over and unallocated from literals so the clamped and typed readings disagree. Add mutation v212-w3-held-unclamped: replace `const v=fsDirVec(it) || {d:p.d, m:p.m};` with a raw read of S.fsrc[id].dv/mv.

I reproduced it at 2bafb12 with my own variant and probes.

The code: fitYearNow reads held as `fsDirVec(it) || {d:p.d, m:p.m}`. fsDirVec clamps a Split's dv/mv to basisSvcOf(it), which is the allocation clamped to the ask. The contract asks for that clamp (recovery/v212/contract.md line 178: "fsDirVec(it) (a Split's typed Disc/Mand, clamped to its basis…"). So the clamp is a requirement, not a builder's choice, and neither notes-W3 nor NEXT-VERSION item 134 records this test gap.

The fixture cannot tell the two readings apart. In w3Board, A's Split dv+mv = [600,200,100] = its ask and B's = [500,300,200] = its ask. The fit block's one edit, A.dv[0]=550 and A.mv[2]=0, stays under the ask. So clamped and raw give identical held figures everywhere.

The variant.
