f.title: Budget Management for a tagged plan says 'The base is read from BES28, live' in a year BES28 does not log, and no check covers that year
f.area: W3 checks (audit-board 'v2.12 W3 — every year’s budget authority…' Budget Management part only opens FY27, a logged year)
f.where: prioritization-board-grid.html bmBody() (`live=!!R.key` → bmLiveRow(R))
f.scenario: The plan is tagged BES28, and FY28 (or any year BES28 has no figure in) is on screen. Budget Management's banner says 'The base is read from BES28, live'. The line under it says 'BES28 logs nothing for FY28: every base is the board’s own', every base is an ordinary box, and 'Take the base from a PPBE position' is withheld. The same happens when the tag has no position for this appropriation at all (R.has false). The banner contradicts what is shown and what is used.
f.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/checks/probes/unsplit-and-bm.mjs, bmFY28: header 'The base is read from BES28, liveBES28 logs nothing for FY28: every base is the board’s own, from Budget Management. …', boxes 2, takeOffered false.
f.fix: Choose bmLiveRow only when R.logged && R.from.indexOf('pos')>=0, or word its heading from fitSrcSay(R). Add a check in the W3 live block on FY29 (logged by nobody): the header, the boxes, and what is offered.

votes.why:
I read the code at 2bafb12 and ran my own probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-checks-4-0/bm-unlogged.mjs (jsdom, 3 services). The finding holds.

The code: bmBody() sets `live=!!R.key` and draws bmLiveRow(R) for any tagged plan. Its heading is a fixed string, 'The base is read from '+lbl+', live'. It never looks at R.logged, R.has or R.from. baOf() sets from[i]='pos' only when `logged` is true (fdcPosHeld on that fiscal year).

What the probe showed:
- **FY29 on screen, plan tagged BES28, BES28 logs FY28 only.** The heading says "The base is read from BES28, live". The hint under it says "BES28 logs nothing for FY29: every base is the board's own". All 6 bases are ordinary boxes and no cell reads from the position; from[] is all 'board'.
- **FY27, the base year, under the same tag.** The result is the same. This case is very likely in real use: a BES28 position logs FY28 onward, and the board opens on FY27.
- **Plan tagged PB27 with no PB27 position at all (R.has false).** This is reachable, because cycLock tags an untagged plan, and so is the PPBE cycles retag. The heading says "The base is read from PB27, live" over "O&M logs no PB27 position".
- **The hint also ends "Untag the plan to type every base here again"**, though every base can already be typed.
- **FY28 (logged) is correct**: 2 position cells, 4 boxes.
- **Untagged (control)**: no live row, and Take is offered.

The rule: NEXT-VERSION item 134 says a year the position does not log "keeps the board's own figure and says so". The contract asks Budget Management to name where the base comes from. The heading names a source the year does not use. neither notes-W3.md nor the contract records a decision on it.

The check gap is real. The only Budget Management checks are audit-board lines 6599-6607, which open FY27 while BES28 logs it, and untagged. No other tool looks at .bmlive.

One part of the finding is not a defect. Withholding 'Take the base from a PPBE position' on a tagged plan is what the contract asks: "Take from a PPBE position stays only for an untagged plan". So the first fix it proposes would break the contract (see corrected).
votes.corrected:
Narrow the finding. When a plan is tagged and the year on screen has no base from the position (R.logged false, or R.has false, or no from[i]==='pos'), bmLiveRow's heading still says 'The base is read from <tag>, live'. This happens on FY29 and on FY27 when BES28 logs only FY28, and on a tag with no position for this appropriation. The hint ends 'Untag the plan to type every base here again' while every base is already a box, so the heading contradicts both the line under it (fitSrcSay) and what is shown.

Withholding 'Take the base from a PPBE position' is not part of the defect: the contract keeps it for untagged plans only. So do not switch to bmPpRow when the year is not logged.

Fix: in bmLiveRow, word the heading from R. One example: 'The plan is tagged BES28 — it logs nothing for FY29' when !R.logged or no service reads from the position. In the same case, drop or reword the 'Untag … again' sentence. Add checks in the W3 block for FY29 (logged by nobody) and for a tag with no position: the heading, 6 boxes, 0 bmpos cells, and Take withheld.

f.title: The W3 position is never in the shape the box writes for an unsplit cycle, so mandatory budget authority silently becoming $0 is unchecked
f.area: W3 checks (w3Board fixture)
f.where: tools/export-audit/audit-board.mjs w3Board() (BES28 is split:false but carries mandatory figures typed with ppSetV(...,'m',...)); prioritization-board-grid.html baOf() / ppSvcFy()
f.scenario: A new position starts unsplit ('One figure per line'). In that mode the box offers only the discretionary field, so a typed total goes into d. Tag the plan to it, and every named service's mandatory budget authority becomes $0, with the whole total in discretionary. Requirements the mandatory lane paid move to discretionary, which also moves the MC shortage, the ◨ view and Plan A. The fit box says only 'Base from BES28 for USAF.' This looks like the 'silent zero' Brad ruled out. The fixture's unsplit position holds mandatory figures (typed through the 'm' writer, which the box shows only in split mode), so it never meets this case. Whether a one-figure position should zero mandatory is Brad's decision; the defect is that nothing checks it or says it.
f.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/checks/probes/unsplit-and-bm.mjs. Board's own base disc 1000 / mand 200, requirement M funded from mandatory. After ppSetV('USAF','_all',2027,'d','1200') with positionSplit false and cycSetWorking('BES',2028): disc [1200], mand [0]; M goes from [dT 0, mT 200] to [200, 0]. fitSays 'Base from BES28 for USAF.'
f.fix: Ask Brad how a one-figure position reads: as discretionary with mandatory $0, or as a total that leaves the board's own lane split. Then add a w3Board year with a position typed in one-figure mode, assert the decided lanes and the sentence the box says, and add a mutation for it.

votes.why:
Reproduced at 2bafb12 with my own probes in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-checks-5-0/.

p1-scenario.mjs drives the real controls on an O&M board (USAF, ANG; own base disc [1000,100], mand [200,20]):
- The PPBE Budget Positions box opens with "One figure per line" checked.
- + add an RCN / EEIC line is clicked, and $1,200 is typed into the box's one FY27 field. Its handler is `ppSetV("USAF",…,2027,"d",this.value)`, so the position stores {d:1200, m:0} with split false.
- `cycSetWorking('BES',2028)` then makes USAF disc 1000→1200 and mand 200→0. Requirement M moves from m 200 to d 200.
- The fit box's year line says "Base from BES28 for USAF · the board's own for ANG…". Its USAF mandatory row is not drawn, because every figure in it is 0.

`baOf` never reads `P.split`; it takes `ppSvcFy` d and m for each named service. The check gap is real but narrower than the title says:

- **What the W3 blocks already hold.** p2-w3block.mjs copies the W3 "read live" block out of audit-board.mjs and runs it on variant boards. Three alternative readings of `baOf`'s line are each caught by the fixture's ANG FY28 checks. In ANG FY28, ANG is named in the unsplit BES28 but logs nothing that year, and its mandatory is asserted $0 over the board's own 110:
  - v1, keep the own mand when the position logs none: 5 checks fail.
  - v2, an unsplit position's empty mandatory keeps the own: 4 fail.
  - v3, an unsplit total split by the own ratio: 7 fail.
  So "mandatory becoming $0 under an unsplit position is unchecked" is false in general.
- **What they do not hold.** v4 changes only the shape the one-figure box writes: a cell with a discretionary figure and no mandatory keeps the board's own mandatory (`if(c.m || !c.d) m[i]=D$(c.m)`). It passes all three W3 blocks, 64 of 64 checks (p3-w3all.mjs). Clean also passes 64 of 64. Recon U10's d-only position sits on a board whose own mand is [0,0,0], so it cannot tell v4 apart either.

Overstated parts:
- **It is not silent.** Budget Management, tagged, prints "Mandatory (base) $0 BES28" read-only.
- **It is not a new behaviour.** Reading a one-figure position as discretionary with mandatory $0 is the contract's rule (`ppSvcFy` d and m). It is also how the pre-v2.12 Take from a PPBE position read the same position: `bmPpVec` gives d [1200], m [0]. It is not the "silent zero" Brad ruled out, which was about a service or year the position does not log.

The open question for Brad is real, and so is the missing check.
votes.corrected:
Narrow the finding. The behaviour follows contract §W3 (`ppSvcFy` d and m), and the pre-v2.12 Take from a PPBE position read an unsplit position the same way. The W3 fixture already asserts $0 mandatory for a named service in a year the unsplit BES28 logs and it does not (ANG FY28 over the board's own 110). That catches a general keep-own-mand reading, a split-aware one and a total-by-ratio one.

What no check holds is the shape the one-figure box writes: a discretionary figure with no mandatory, over a non-zero own mandatory. A board that kept the own mandatory there passes all 64 W3 checks.

It is not silent: Budget Management shows "Mandatory (base) $0 BES28". But the fit box hides that lane, and the positions box does not say a one-figure cycle reads as discretionary only.

Fix:
1. Ask Brad how a one-figure position reads.
2. Add a w3Board year typed through the box's one field in one-figure mode, with a non-zero own mand. Assert the decided lanes and what the boxes say.
3. Add the mutation `m[i]=D$(c.m)` → `if(c.m || !c.d) m[i]=D$(c.m)`.

votes.why:
The board does what the finding describes, but its main claim is wrong: the behaviour is already checked, and it is what the contract asks for.

What I reproduced at 2bafb12 (probe `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-checks-5-1/unsplit.mjs`). It drives the PPBE box through its rendered controls: add an RCN line, type the codes, type 1200 into the FY27 box with a real change event, then tag the plan with `cycSetWorking`.
- In "One figure" mode, all 7 inputs call `ppSetV(..., 'd', ...)` and are titled "FY2027 Discretionary".
- After tagging, USAF reads disc 1200 and mand 0 (it was 1000 / 200).
- On the lane walk, M's 200 moves from mandatory to discretionary. The fit box line is "Base from BES28 for USAF · the board's own for ANG…". Its table leaves out USAF's all-zero mandatory row. The tag message says only "Working plan tagged BES28".
- It is also true that the `w3Board` BES28 position is `split:false` but holds mandatory figures typed through the 'm' writer.

Why it is refuted:
1. **The reading is checked.** I built each reading the finding offers as a variant of `baOf` (in memory, `alts.mjs`, same folder) and replayed the `w3Board` fixture word for word. Both are caught by the existing 'tagged BES28' FY27 and FY28 expectations, on that same `split:false` position:
   - "a one-figure position leaves the board's own mandatory": FY27 reads mand 200 for 300, and FY28 ANG reads 110 for $0. The FY28 ANG check already pins a named service's empty mandatory at $0, against a board base of 110.
   - "a one-figure position is a total, re-split by the board's own lanes": FY27 reads 1150 / 433600 / … and fails.
   - Only an artificial rule survives: "a lane at 0 next to a lane with a figure keeps the board's own". It contradicts the box's own text: "a line that is discretionary-only simply has nothing in its Mandatory row".
2. **The "should" is the contract's.** The contract says each named service "takes `ppSvcFy(P, sv, fy)` d and m". The one-figure field has always been "the discretionary slot" (code comment, input title). Before v2.12, Take from a PPBE position (`bmSeedFromPp`/`bmPpVec`) read it the same way. The builder wrote down the rule that a named service in a logged year reads the position's $0. Item 134's "never a silent zero" is about "an untagged plan, or a year or service the position does not log". Here the position does log the service, and no money is lost: total budget authority is the 1200 typed.
3. **It is not silent.** Budget Management shows "$0 BES28" for USAF mandatory, with "The board's own base, $200, stays underneath" in its tooltip. Every requirement now carries a Split by default, and on a Split the mandatory it holds becomes an over. In my split variant that is flagged as "🏛 1 over BES28" in Needs attention, with the fit box showing USAF mandatory $0 BES28, held 200, over 200. Nothing is flagged only for a requirement still on the lane walk (older boards). There the total funded is unchanged and the money only changes lane.

What is left is a product question: should tagging to a one-figure position warn that its figures are read as discretionary? That is for Brad. It is not a gap in the checks.
votes.corrected: True as stated: a position typed in the default "One figure" mode writes only the discretionary slot, so tagging the plan reads each named service's mandatory budget authority as the position's $0. That follows the contract (`ppSvcFy` d and m) and how the box has always stored that field. The existing W3 checks already pin it. On the split:false BES28 fixture, the FY27 and FY28 'tagged BES28' expectations fail both ways a one-figure position could otherwise be read: keeping the board's own mandatory (FY28 ANG 110 instead of $0), and re-splitting a total by the board's lanes. The board also shows it: "$0 BES28" in Budget Management, and an over flag for any Split holding mandatory money. Only requirements still on the lane walk change lane with no flag. Whether tagging should also warn is an open question for Brad, worth a note, not a missing check.

dropped.title: A header row repeated below the one read is parsed as data: its year titles become dollars, and its '$ Type' title passes the then-year test
dropped.why:
The mechanism is real, but the scenario is not one the board meets, and the behaviour is what the contract specifies.

**What I reproduced.** I wrote my own probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-6-0/probe.mjs. It booted the board at 2bafb12 and imported, through `importAce`, a workbook built with `buildXlsx`. The workbook had a Cover sheet and a title row, then the header on sheet row 3 repeated verbatim on row 4, then one real line. I ran three versions: with and without US/PTN/FMS, and with the year headers as numbers and as text.
- In every version the repeated row was read as data.
- Its years read as dollars: 2026 became $2,026,000,000 and 2027 became $2,027,000,000.
- `thenYear` was 2. `aceTitleN('$ Type')` is 'type', which passes `dt.indexOf('ty')===0` at line 14948.
- The row was left out as 'partner' when US/PTN/FMS was present, and as 'jpo' when it was absent.
- The report printed "Left out: Partner or FMS … 1 $2,027,000,000 $4,053,000,000" and a sheet total of $4,056,000,000. `rep.ties` was still true.

**Why I refute it.**

1. **Not a file ORBIT really meets.**
   - Brad's 2026 file has a single header row, on row 3 of PMO Database Output (NEXT-VERSION item 132).
   - The "printed layout's repeat" trigger does not exist. Excel's repeat-on-print rows are a defined name (`_xlnm.Print_Titles`), not sheet rows. The board's own writer stores them that way (line 29689), and `xlsxRead` reads only sheetData, so it never sees a repeat.
   - A second header line that repeats every title verbatim is contrived. No file, note or request describes one.

2. **The 'should' is not what the contract asks.**
   - Contract rule 2 defines then-year as "normalised value starts `ty`, or reads `then year`". Line 14948 implements exactly that.
   - Rule 1 defines not-data as "no WBS and no dollar in any year column".
   - Neither the contract nor item 132 has a rule about a repeated header. The proposed header test and the exact TY regex are new requirements, not a deviation by the builder. notes-W1 records no different decision.

3. **The impact is cosmetic and conspicuous even if it were reached.**
   - The repeated row can never be kept. Its own 'JPO Managed' cell fails rule 7, and its 'US/PTN/FMS' cell fails rule 6. So no dollar reaches a line, the tie-out, the Spruills or FYDP Disconnects; my probe kept exactly the one real line.
   - Only the import report's left-out and sheet totals carry an absurd $2B-a-year row, which a reader would spot at once.
   - A file holding no then-year rows is still refused. Its message changes from naming the dollar types to "every row was left out".

At most this is a hardening suggestion, not a defect. | The mechanics reproduce at 2bafb12, but the finding does not hold up as a defect. I wrote my own probe at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-6-1/probe.mjs. It builds the workbook with the board's own buildXlsx and imports it through the real importAce path.

What reproduces: with the titles repeated on the row under the real header, aceParse (loop at line 14938) reads that row as data. Its year titles become $2,024,000,000 to $2,028,000,000, and its '$ Type' cell normalises to 'type', which passes `dt.indexOf('ty')===0`. The report then shows 'Left out: Partner or FMS … 1 row, $10,130,000,000'. With the US/PTN/FMS column removed, the same row lands under 'Not JPO managed' instead.

Why it does not stand:
1. **Nothing shows a real file reaches it.** Brad's 2026 file has its titles on row 3 of PMO Database Output and data under them (NEXT-VERSION item 132). No real file, item or note describes a repeated title row. One of the two triggers named, 'a printed layout's repeat', cannot happen: Excel's repeated print rows are a defined name (`_xlnm.Print_Titles`), not cells. The board's reader reads sheetData only. The other trigger, a second header line repeating the same titles, is invented for the probe.
2. **The then-year 'should' contradicts the contract.** recovery/v212/contract.md W1 step 2 sets the rule as 'normalised value starts `ty`, or reads `then year`'. The code does exactly that. The proposed exact regex would change the contract rather than fix a departure from it.
3. **No figure ORBIT uses moves.** A title row can never be kept. 'JPO Managed' normalises to 'jpomanaged', which fails the Yes test. 'PMO' is not an office. 'US/PTN/FMS' reads as partner. So it always falls into a left-out reason. In all three runs the kept lines and the appropriation, PMO and service totals were identical to the control. The report still ties ('Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in one reason'). Only the report's left-out section and its sheet total carry the made-up row.
4. **A file with no then-year rows is still refused.** It gets past the no-then-year check but is then refused as 'every row was left out'.

At most this is an optional hardening idea: skip a row under the header whose aceHdrScore is at least ACE_HDR_MIN. It is not a reachable defect against the contract or items 132 and 134.

dropped.title: A renamed US/PTN/FMS column is 'not in this file', never asked about, and every partner and FMS line is kept as the JPO's estimate
dropped.why:
The behaviour is real, but it is what the contract specifies, so it is not a defect in the build. I reproduced it with my own probe, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w1-parse-7-0/probe.mjs, which uses a minimal titled workbook and the board's own buildXlsx and importAce. Its three FY27 rows are US $1M, FMS $5M and PTN $7M.
- **Column titled US/PTN/FMS:** 1 line is kept ($1,000,000), and "partner" holds 2 rows and $12,000,000.
- **Column titled US/Partner/FMS:** the mapping box does not open (aceColOpen false), 3 lines are kept ($13,000,000), there is no partner reason, and rep.absent includes usptn. The status line reads "No row left out. Every dollar of the sheet is kept or in a reason." The only mention is in the folded "Columns read, by title" details: "Not in this file (they name nothing): …, US/PTN/FMS".

dropped.title: Every year's budget authority and funded figures change with no message when a pre-v2.12 tagged board is opened, or when the plan is retagged to a cycle with no position
dropped.why:
I reproduced the mechanics at 2bafb12 with my own probes (pa.mjs and pb.mjs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w3-live-1-0/). They do not show a defect against what was asked.

What reproduced:
- (1) A board saved by the slot build (v2.11, d732259), tagged BES28 with a BES28 position, opened in 2bafb12 reads the position. FY27 USAF went from 1000/200 to 300/10, FY28 from 1100/210 to 5000/700, and FY27 funded from 2050 to 1160. The status line is only "Opened with the saved board state…", and DIRTY, _baseDirty and unsavedNow are all false.
- (2) Lock BES28, then the status line's Retag button: PB28 has no position, so both years go back to the board's own base. The status line reads "🏷 Working plan tagged PB28 — deltas read against BES28".

Why it is not a defect:
- **The figures are meant to move.** NEXT-VERSION item 134 (Brad's decisions 1 and 2, and the proposal) says a tagged plan's every year IS the position, read live, and "retagging the plan (BES28 to PB28) moves every year to the new position". The guide's t-ppbe section says the same: "Retag the plan and every year moves to the new position."
- **Nothing marked unsaved on opening is the contract's own rule.** contract.md §W3 says: "Opening and refreshing write nothing on their own (no save(), no unsaved mark): the caches are derived." notes-W3.md records it as a decision ("a file … opens live, unsaved-mark untouched (checked)").
- **No message on opening, retag or lock is asked for anywhere.** Not by the contract, not by item 134, not by CLAUDE.md. Item 134's "keeps the board's own figure and says so" is about naming the source, and the board does that. Budget Management, where the base is shown, opens with bmLiveRow → fitSrcSay. After the retag it read "O&M logs no PB28 position: every base is the board's own, from Budget Management". After opening it read "Base from BES28 for USAF · the board's own for ANG, AFRC". The fit box names the source year by year. So the finding's "said only inside the fit box" is wrong.

The finding also overstates two things:
- **Lock:** cycLock's question already tells an untagged plan, before it happens: "this lock tags it BES28, and from then on every year BES28 logs reads its budget authority from the BES28 position" (only when baPosHas).
- **"The next Save bakes the new figures in":** S.bm.disc and S.bm.mand are never overwritten. The saved discSvc and mandSvc are derived and are worked out again on every v2.12 opening, and untagging gives the board's own base back to the dollar.

A one-time notice on upgrade (as W1's PSM heal gives) or on retag would be a reasonable enhancement. It is not a requirement the code fails. | I reproduced the facts with my own probes on the 2bafb12 board (q1.mjs and q2.mjs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w3-live-1-1/). They do not make it a defect against what was asked.

What reproduces:
- Probe 1: a board saved by v2.11 (d732259), tagged BES28, with USAF FY27 logged at 300/10, then opened in 2bafb12. The FY27 cache goes from [1000,400,300]/[200,100,50] to [300,400,300]/[10,100,50] and funded from 2,050 to 1,160. The status line is only "Opened with the saved board state…", STAT_LOG holds only that line, and DIRTY is false.
- Probe 2: after the lock, cycRetagNext moves FY27 and FY28 back to the board's own base. Its status line is only "Working plan tagged PB28 — deltas read against BES28".

Why it is not a defect:
1. The money moving is the requested behaviour. NEXT-VERSION item 134 says "All years should reference the PPBE Budget assigned" and "retagging the plan (BES28 to PB28) moves every year to the new position".
2. The silence and the clean unsaved state are the contract's own decision. Contract § W3: "Opening and refreshing write nothing on their own (no save(), no unsaved mark): the caches are derived." It also says the record of where each base came from is "for the panels". notes-W3 records that "a file saved with a stale cache opens live, unsaved-mark untouched (checked)". Nothing in the contract or item 134 asks for a status-line or opening message when the budget moves. Brad's decision 3 asks that an overage be flagged, and the 🏛 Needs attention entry does that.
3. "Said only inside the fit box" is false. bmLiveRow in Budget Management prints fitSrcSay. On the retagged plan it reads "O&M logs no PB28 position: every base is the board's own, from Budget Management". On the opened board it reads "Base from BES28 for USAF · the board's own for ANG, AFRC".
4. The cycLock part is false. When an untagged plan is locked, the confirm says first: "The working plan is untagged: this lock tags it BES28, and from then on every year BES28 logs reads its budget authority from the BES28 position…". This holds whenever baPosHas(key); when the tag logs no position, nothing moves.
5. "The next Save bakes the new figures in" is false. S.bm.disc and S.bm.mand are never overwritten. The file saved by 2bafb12 still holds FY27 bm [1000,400,300]/[200,100,50], and only the derived discSvc/mandSvc caches change. Untagging restored the exact figures and funded 2,050.

No data is lost and no figure is wrong. What remains is a suggestion to also announce the move in the status line. That is beyond the contract, and "major" overstates it.

Reproduced with my own probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w3-live-2-0/probe1.mjs), run on the board taken from git at 2bafb12 and driven through the board's own setters (cycSetWorking, ppSetV):
- Untagged, the FY28 cache is [[1100,410,310],[210,110,60]] and ANG's FY28 funded total is 500.
- With the plan tagged BES28, USAF FY27 and ANG FY27 typed, nothing changes.
- When USAF FY28 is typed, the FY28 cache becomes [[5000,0,310],[700,0,60]], BA_SRC.from is [pos,pos,board], and ANG's FY28 funded total is 0.
- The fit box's FY28 line reads "Base from BES28 for USAF, ANG · the board's own for AFRC". The FY28 table omits ANG's rows because they are all zero.

So the code does exactly what the finding describes. It is reachable by a person who tags the plan and then fills the position one service at a time.

But the "should" is not what the build was asked for:
- recovery/v212/contract.md § W3 says that when the position "logs that year (any cell in that year, as fdcPosHeld), each service the position names takes ppSvcFy(P, sv, fy) d and m". Only "a service it does not name, a year it does not log, or an untagged plan" keeps the board's own base. ANG is named (FY27) and FY28 is logged (USAF), so ANG FY28 takes BES28's $0.
- NEXT-VERSION item 134's "a year or service the position does not log" has the same year-or-service structure. The contract resolved that wording at the year level, and the finding's per-cell reading is a different interpretation.
- Brad's own quoted words ("pull from those year's totals I've posted") do not settle it either.
- The builder documented this exact case, with the reason, in the comment above baNamed() and under "Decided in the build" in notes-W3.md. ppSetV deletes a typed 0, so a blank and a 0 cannot be told apart. Under the finding's rule, a person could not give a service $0 in a year at all.
- The finding itself says "This needs Brad's call".
- It is not silent. The year's source line names ANG as based on BES28, and the PPBE Budget Positions box shows the ANG FY28 cell blank.

At most this is a design question to put to Brad, not a confirmed defect at 2bafb12. | The behaviour is real, but it is not a defect against the stated requirements.

What reproduces: I wrote my own probe (`/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/792dafeb-d944-5a2a-8cfa-66d1840065b4/scratchpad/rv212/verify-w3-live-2-1/v1.mjs`) at 2bafb12. BES28 logs USAF FY27 and FY28, and ANG FY27 only. After `cycSetWorking('BES',2028)` the FY28 cache goes from [[1100,410,310],[210,110,60]] to [[5000,0,310],[0,0,60]]. ANG funded in FY28 is 0. `BA_SRC[2028].from` is ["pos","pos","board"], and the fit line reads "Base from BES28 for USAF, ANG · the board's own for AFRC". `ppSetV` deletes a typed 0 (the ANG FY28 cell is gone afterwards). A person can reach this while building a position service by service.

Why it is refuted:

1. **The contract asks for it in so many words.** contract.md § W3 says that for a year the position logs ("any cell in that year, as fdcPosHeld"), "each service the position names (ppSvcsOf) takes ppSvcFy(P, sv, fy)". That gives exactly $0 here. W3 narrowed "names" (`baNamed`: a figure in some year) so that an empty placeholder line cannot zero a service.

2. **The builder documented it and tests it.** notes-W3.md › Decided in the build says that a named service with nothing in a logged year reads the position's $0, because `ppSetV` deletes a zero. audit-board's W3 block asserts it: "ANG named and logged nothing for FY28 ($0)" → [[5075,0,310],[700,0,60]].

3. **The board's own vocabulary reads "a service the position does not log" at service level, and item 134 keeps that vocabulary.** The rule item 134 replaces is `bmPpVec`/`bmSeedFromPp`. It treats every service in `ppSvcsOf` as "covered" for any year and takes `ppSvcFy`=0 for a year with no cell. The old Take from a PPBE position would also have set ANG FY28 410→0, naming it in its confirm. Its comment "says nothing about this service - NOT the same as zero" is about the service, not the service-in-year. NEXT-VERSION's "What is there today" describes that same rule ("A service the position says nothing about is left as it was"). FYDP Disconnects reads it the same way too (`fdcPosHeld` is true, ANG `ppSvcFy` is 0). Here the year is logged and ANG is logged, so neither half of "a year or service the position does not log" applies.

4. **It is not silent.** Budget Management on FY28 shows ANG as "$0 BES28". Its title reads "read from BES28 for FY28 in PPBE Budget Positions — change it there. The board's own base, $410, stays underneath…". The fit box names BES28 as the source. So "says its base is from the position" is accurate: BES28's own FY28 total counts ANG at $0.

5. **The alternative breaks another stated rule.** Since a blank cannot be told from a typed 0, keeping the board's own base would read a deliberately typed $0 as $410. The budget would then sit above the position, against item 134's "no report states more than the position".

The proposed fix changes `ppSetV`'s storage format (v2.06 items 119/120) and changes the contract's rule. As the finding itself says, that is a design question for Brad, not a defect in the build.
